newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Keppel, PSA in joint land development.
newsitem.headline: Keppel, PSA in joint land development.

text.p: Diversified maritime group Keppel Corp Ltd and the Port of Singapore Authority (PSA) said on Monday they have signed a memorandum of understanding to jointly develop adjacent lands in western Singapore.
The area comprises 32 hectares of Keppel waterfront land including an island, Pulau Keppel, and PSA's 20.3 hectares of mixed land use at Maritime Square, a joint statement said.
Maritime Square, with a current plot ratio of one, encompasses the World Trade Centre, Cable Car Towers, Singapore Cruise Centre, Expo Halls and car parks.

According to PSA president Khoo Teng Chye, the decision to redevelop its site was triggered by plans to demolish two exhibition halls in the area to make way for a planned Mass Rapid Transport (MRT) station.
"An opportunity now exists for us to take a fresh look at how the area can be redeveloped...As a result, PSA decided to begin the masterplan," Khoo told a news briefing.
And as PSA shares a common boundary of eight to nine hectares with Keppel, Khoo said it decided to jointly develop its site with Keppel.
"Keppel is a property developer, PSA is not," Khoo said.
According to Keppel senior executive director Lim Chee Onn, the two were in talks to develop the common boundary.
"But for the rest of the development, it's up to PSA as to how it wants to be involved," Lim said.
Khoo said PSA was still drawing up its masterplan.
"The MOU is a broad statement of cooperation. Exactly how is not decided yet. It will be finalised later," Khoo said.

Keppel, which had long mooted the idea of redeveloping its site, felt the strategic alliance with PSA would enable it to provide "a unique product on the waterfront" and the two developments were unlikely to be in competition.

Lim said Keppel had applied for planning approval to develop its site into a waterfront condominium with marina facilities and offices, while PSA's plans were for a maritime centre including a cruise centre with related maritime activities.

When completed, Keppel's project would yield a total gross floor area of about 435,000 square metres, of which 89 percent would be for residential use, nine percent for offices and shops and two percent for a marina club and marina, Lim said.
Development work on the Keppel site is expected to start as soon as possible and to be completed in three to four phases over at least eight years.
Its residential project was targeted to be launched sometime in late 1998, depending on market conditions, Lim said.

While unable to disclose Keppel's total development costs, as land cost and premium were yet to be determined, Lim said its construction cost was estimated at Singapore $1.2 to $1.3 billion, based on market prices.
On Keppel's funding plans, Lim said it would be financed by the group's internal funds, bank borrowings and part of the proceeds from its preferential share issue.
He did not rule out the possibility of bringing other Keppel subsidiaries into the project.
PSA's Khoo said the group hopes to see the first phase of its development completed in tandem with the completion of the MRT station in year 2002.
